summary: Wicomico County, MD steel fire tower built 1943 with US Navy funds, 140 ft; NHLR-registered 2017 when DNR planned removal; now listed as gone.

facts.status_note: Forest Fire Lookout Association Maryland list marks it Tower Gone, undated; the 2017 NHLR entry says DNR planned to remove it. No removal date or site description found.

events.note: Built with US Navy funds during WWII, for fire detection and as an aircraft and watercraft warning site
Maryland DNR planned to remove the tower, per the NHLR entry as of 2017

evidence.quote: was built using US Navy funds during World War II for both fire detection and as an aircraft and watercraft warning service site

evidence.quote: At 140 feet, this steel tower is the tallest in Maryland

notes_for_editor: The brief's status 'gone' rests on the undated Maryland list (source 2); the 2017 NHLR entry only says removal was planned, so the removal date is unknown and the story does not give one. The brief's elevation (12.8 m, from NHLR's 42 ft figure) is not a facts key and was not used. No source found on staffing, fires, or the site today. Read budget exceeded (about 12 page reads, many dead ends: Wikipedia, MHT survey PDF, DNR poster, a Powellville fire company page); 2 searches used. Fact-check 2026-10-09: Wicomico County added as an evidence quote; the DNR paragraph's copied wording was rewritten; the story now says none of the sources checked describes the site, rather than no source.
